title: Vilasa 9. Jahnava in Vrindavana; Her Return through Kheturi; the Brahmana Healed of Leprosy
html:
Jahnava's journey to Vrindavana, her meeting with the Gosvamis, her tour of Vraja; Gopinatha in a dream asks her to send Him Radha; Jahnava's return through Kheturi, Budhari, Katwa, Yajigrama and Shrikhanda; Srinivasa and Narottama teach; the offending brahmana struck with leprosy is forgiven by Narottama

1Glory to Gaura, Nityananda and Advaita with their associates!
Be merciful, Prabhu, to this wretched beggar.

2Glory, glory to the listeners, oceans of mercy!
Hear what I shall now relate.

3Sri Jahnava Ishvari, going from the village of Kheturi to Vrindavana,
performed an unearthly deed.

4What shall I say? Wicked pashandis and yavanas
effortlessly obtained the rare treasure of bhakti.

5Those who kept company with such people —
they too became intoxicated with Sri Krishna Chaitanya's virtues.

6Along whatever road the Ishvari went with everyone,
the people of those lands ran along with her.

7In whatever village she stayed for a day,
the villagers' joy was boundless.

8So, destroying the impurity of so many beings,
she went by way of Prayaga quickly to Madhupuri.1

9Bathing with everyone at the Sri Vishrama-ghata,
she honoured the brahmanas of Sri Mathura.

10Staying there that day and night, and bathing in the morning,
the Ishvari joyfully went on from there.

11That the Ishvari had come to Mathura
everyone everywhere heard.

12All the Gosvamis quickly, with gladness of heart,
came out from Vrindavana to meet her.

13Meanwhile the Ishvari with everyone, from afar,
gazed overwhelmed at the sweetness of the forest.

14Unable to check her tears, drenched with them,
she got down from the palanquin and went on foot.

15Sri Parameshvara Dasa, before the Ishvari,
spoke softly in the sweetest words:

16"Sri Gopala Bhatta, Sri Bhugarbha, Lokanatha,
Sri Jiva, Sri Krishna Pandita and others together —

17all these have come out to meet you."
Saying this, he pointed them all out from afar.

18Seeing them all, Sri Jahnava Ishvari
became such as I cannot tell.

19All the Gosvamis, at the sight of the Ishvari,
lost their composure and could not check their tears.

20Falling to the ground and bowing at the Ishvari's feet,
they could not say anything of all that rose in their hearts.

21With Krishnadasa Sarakhela, Madhava Acharya and all the others
the meeting took place as was fitting.

22Sri Parameshvara Dasa, taking Govinda and others,
brought them together and introduced everyone.

23Sri Govinda Kaviraja and all the others
bowed to the ground at the Gosvamis' feet.

24All, with great mercy toward them,
embraced them with gladness of heart.

25How that meeting was —
for fear of the book's length it is not told in detail.

26Sri Jiva Gosvami, saying many things carefully,
seating the Ishvari in a palanquin carried by men,

27quickly led everyone to a secluded lodging;
people ran from all sides to see the Ishvari.

28From Sri Govinda, Gopinatha, Madanamohana
their servants came from there.

29Who was doing what, no one remembered;
what wondrous bliss there was in Vrindavana!

30When the Ishvari with everyone had settled in the lodging,
all the food was brought there.

31Quickly feeding everyone with various prasada delicacies,
the Ishvari ate a little herself.

32Sri Gopala Bhatta and others, with gladness of heart,
took leave and went to their own dwellings.

33For the darshan of Govinda's raja-bhoga arati
all went together with Sri Jiva Gosvami.

34Sri Jahnava Ishvari, entering the temple,
lost her composure on seeing Radha-Govinda.

35Sri Madhava Acharya and others, at the sight of Govinda,
were overwhelmed; tears streamed from their eyes.

36They saw the arati of Sri Govinda
and with great joy honoured the maha-prasada.

37Coming back from there, all rested,
and Sri Jiva Gosvami went joyfully to his dwelling.

38In the afternoon Sri Jahnava Ishvari
quickly bathed with everyone.

39Going to the temples of Madanamohana and Gopinatha,
she had darshan, overwhelmed with prema.

40Sri Radha-vinoda, Sri Radharamana,
Radha-Damodara — she saw them all.

41The transformations of bhava at these darshans —
how can I, a wretch, describe them with one mouth?

42The various cloths and ornaments she had brought
she offered everywhere.

43What shall I say of the bliss in eating the prasada
of Sri Govinda, Gopinatha and Madanamohana?

44Before Lokanatha and the others they told everything:
how the great festival in Kheturi had been,

45how they had come along the road — they told it all,
and hearing it, all the Gosvamis rejoiced.

46All the Gosvamis, gathering their composure,
told what had happened to them.

47Hearing it, the Ishvari's heart was distraught,
and Madhava Acharya and others could not contain themselves.

48After a while, growing calm, all said:
"Please hear some of Govinda's poetry."

49Hearing Govinda's verses, they praised them greatly,
and the title "Kaviraja" was approved by all.2

50Sri Ishvari, with their permission,
went to Sri Kunda by way of Bahulavana.

51Those who had come from Sri Kunda
all went along with the Ishvari.

52Having seen Radha-kunda and Shyama-kunda,
they saw Sri Manasa-Ganga and Govardhana.

53By way of Vrishabhanupura they went to Nandishvara
and saw the lovely village of Sri Javat.

54Seeing the place where Balarama performed the rasa-lila,
they came back to Vrindavana.

55For Sri Govinda, Gopinatha, Madanamohana,
Sri Radha-vinoda and Sri Radharamana,

56and Sri Radha-Damodara — for all of them the Ishvari carefully
cooked and offered food in turn.

57What bliss arose in the hearts of all the Gosvamis
as they ate that prasada — who knows?

58So Sri Jahnava stayed some days,
and Sri Jiva Gosvami read her something from his books.

59Again the Ishvari, taking everyone with her,
went in turn around the twelve forests.

60What bliss there was on which day in which place —
for fear of the book's length it is not described.

61She made ready to travel to Gauda,
and all the Gosvamis gave their consent.

62Sri Govinda, Gopinatha, Madanamohana,
Radha-Damodara and Sri Radharamana,

63Sri Radha-vinoda — from all of them
she took leave, telling what was in her heart.

64What the Ishvari became at the parting
could not be described even with a thousand mouths.

65Madhava Acharya and others calmed themselves with effort,
and that day all stayed in Vrindavana.

66The dearest disciple of Gauridasa Pandita,
named Bara Gangadasa, incomparable in virtue,

67had come to Vrindavana earlier;
he never stayed in one place but always wandered.

68The Ishvari herself, showing him mercy,
commanded: "You will go with me to Gauda."

69Receiving such a command, he made ready.
Meanwhile Govinda and others went to the Gosvamis' dwellings.

70Bowing at the feet of Sri Gopala Bhatta and Lokanatha,
they told what was in their hearts.

71Sri Bhatta and Sri Lokanatha were very pleased
and blessed Srinivasa and Narottama.

72Placing their feet on the heads of all,
what more they said cannot be described.

73From there they went to the dwelling of Bhugarbha Gosvami,
and he showed them all great mercy.

74From there they went to Jiva Gosvami;
Krishnadasa Kaviraja and others were there.

75At once they saw many together,
and falling to the ground they bowed at the feet of all.

76All showed them great mercy;
Sri Jiva Gosvami said affectionately to Govinda:

77"Tell the Acharya the news from here
and send me the nectar of the songs you have composed.

78I shall finish this book very soon
and send the book with a man, together with a letter."

79Saying this, he gave them the Gopala-virudavali,3
and Krishnadasa Kaviraja and others praised it.

80So, having visited everywhere,
they came quickly back to the lodging and rested.

81When the Ishvari lay down late at night,
Gopinatha appeared to her in a dream.

82He gave Jahnava the garland from His own neck
and, smiling softly, said slowly:

83"What you resolved on seeing My Beloved,
go to Gauda and quickly send it.

84She will be on the left, and this one on the right;
the beauty that will be — you will see it."4

85Saying many such things, He went into the temple;
when the sleep broke, she saw what she had seen.

86Keeping Sri Gopinatha's garland hidden,
she went for the darshan of the Sri mangala-arati.

87Having seen the arati and offered many prayers,
she came back to the lodging, greatly rejoicing.

88When the night turned to morning, at a very auspicious moment,
Sri Ishvari set out from the lodging.

89All the Gosvamis came there;
what they said cannot be described.

90Having gone some distance, all, at the Ishvari's command,
took leave, bathed in streams of tears.

91Sri Jahnava Ishvari could not be calm:
tears flowed from her eyes like the current of a river.

92Krishnadasa Pandita, Sri Madhava Acharya,
Murari Chaitanya and others lost their composure.

93They wept, and the people of Vraja wept;
having gone some distance, all grew calm.

94The people of Vraja went to their dwellings,
and Sri Ishvari with everyone came to Mathura.

95That day she stayed in Mathura
and carefully fed the brahmanas of Mathura.

96From there she set out for Gauda
and after some days came to the village of Kheturi.

97Hearing from people of the Ishvari's coming,
Narottama forgot himself for joy.

98Calling Ramachandra, he told him the news;
hearing of her coming, all rejoiced.

99They went out to meet her with their people,
and the people of the village of Kheturi ran from all sides.

100Going some distance, they saw a wondrous procession,
and the meeting took place in great bliss.

101They fell rolling at the Ishvari's feet,
and the Ishvari rejoiced to see them all.

102Casting a merciful glance on the people of Kheturi,
she entered the village of Kheturi with everyone.

103Sri Ishvari stayed in her former lodging,
and many people were appointed to serve.

104Sri Govinda Kaviraja and all the others gladly
stayed in their former lodgings.

105Baru Gangadasa and the other wise ones
stayed there, finding a wonderful secluded place.

106Ramachandra Kaviraja with great care
took various provisions to every place.

107Before the Ishvari, Sri Thakura Mahashaya
begged her again and again to bathe.

108Quickly bathing in warm water and doing her rites,
the Ishvari ate a few prasada sweets.

109Quickly cooking, she offered it to Prabhu,
and when He ate, everyone was glad.

110So all the mahantas bathed and so on,
and Sri Santosha dressed them all in new cloths.

111All ate the prasada sweets,
and meanwhile food was quickly cooked in one place.

112The cooks, having offered the food to Krishna,
joyfully fed all the mahantas.

113Sri Govinda Kaviraja and all the others
ate together with the cooks.

114All chewed prasada betel
and lay down for a little while in their own places.

115Baru Gangadasa and others, going to their own place,
rested for a while, happily.

116Sri Ishvari, having rested a while,
quickly bathed and did her rites again.

117Narottama, with Ramachandra, Santosha and others,
came with joyful hearts to Sri Ishvari.

118At the Ishvari's command all sat on their seats;
Narottama wished to ask something.

119Knowing what was in his heart, Jahnava Ishvari
told in detail of her journey to Vrindavana and so on.

120Reflecting on the doings of all the Gosvamis,
she lost her composure; streams flowed from her eyes.

121After a while, growing calm, she consoled everyone
and told by hints of Sri Gopinatha's command —

122that she must go quickly. When she made this known,
Ramachandra Kaviraja said with joined palms:

123"We had hoped you would stay here some days —
our wish has come to nothing."

124The Ishvari said: "I can say nothing;
consider and tell me what is right, and I shall do it."

125Sri Thakura Mahashaya said slowly:
"In two or four days set out for Khardaha.

126It is better that the image be made in your presence;
in such matters there must be no delay.

127On the road you will be delayed some days;
tomorrow morning I shall send a man to Khardaha."

128Saying this, in Sri Jahnava Ishvari's presence
he had a letter written and gave it into Santosha's hand.

129He wrote a letter to Acharya Thakura too
and quickly sent a messenger with the two letters.

130It was time for the darshan of the evening arati,
and they went with Sri Ishvari to Prabhu's courtyard.

131Sri Madhava Acharya and all the others came quickly
and joyfully saw Prabhu's arati.

132Sri Jahnava Ishvari, entering the temple,
had darshan — what did she say to Him by a hint?

133For a while she listened to the kirtana,
and Sri Ishvari went to her own lodging.

134Madhava Acharya and all the others went to their lodgings,
and Ramachandra and others remained in Prabhu's courtyard.

135Quickly taking Prabhu's prasada delicacies,
they fed everyone with the greatest care.

136Tired from the road, all lay down,
and Sri Santosha and others massaged their feet.

137Ramachandra went quickly to the Ishvari
and gave her a little prasada milk to drink.

138All the brahmanas' wives who were with Sri Ishvari
he carefully fed a little.

139When Sri Ishvari had lain down, the Mahashaya
came with Ramachandra to Prabhu's house.

140Taking Ramachandra, Govinda and all the others,
the Mahashaya joyfully ate prasada.

141Finding the moment, to Thakura Mahashaya
Sri Govinda Kaviraja carefully reported

142what all the Gosvamis had bidden him say,
and having said it, gave him the Gopala-virudavali.

143Hearing it, the Mahashaya fell silent
and lost his composure in a way I cannot tell.

144After a while, consoling himself, he grew calm
and gave the Gopala-virudavali to Ramachandra.

145Still he lay down distraught,
and in a dream Lokanatha appeared to him.

146Narottama, falling at the Gosvami's feet,
drenched his lotus feet with the tears of his eyes.

147The Gosvami embraced Narottama
and spoke nectarean words of consolation.

148Giving Narottama great joy,
smiling softly, he vanished.

149Sri Thakura Mahashaya was greatly delighted
and passed the rest of the night chanting the holy name.

150All, having done their morning duties, with Narottama
became absorbed in talk of Sri Vrindavana.

151So in great bliss they spent four days;
as before, the Ishvari cooked and so on.

152The bliss she manifested in those four days —
who could describe it? The fortunate saw it.

153Sri Thakura Mahashaya with Ramachandra
together fixed the time of departure.

154Sri Govinda Kaviraja and some others
they sent with supreme joy to Budhari.

155Sri Santosha said: "The departure is tomorrow morning —
quickly make preparations for the journey."

156To all the pujaris he said with great care:
"Be attentive in the service of Prabhu and the Vaishnavas."

157So he instructed everyone in every task
and reported it all to Sri Ishvari.

158Meanwhile Sri Santosha Raya and some others
quickly made preparations for the journey.

159What was fitting to send with Sri Ishvari
he entrusted to Sri Parameshvara Dasa.

160When the night turned to morning, into Prabhu's courtyard
all came to take leave.

161Seeing Prabhu, all, with gladness of heart,
offered many prayers in soft words.

162The pujari gave everyone prasada garlands and cloths,
and all, bowing to the ground, took leave.

163Sri Jahnava Ishvari, losing composure at the darshan,
took leave — what did she say within herself?

164Bowing, placing the garland and cloth on her head,
she went out of the courtyard with everyone.

165Sri Thakura Mahashaya took leave
and bowed, reciting a verse of his own composition.

166Thus:
O Gauranga, Vallavikanta, Sri Krishna, Vrajamohana,
Radharamana, O Radha, Radhakanta — obeisance to You!

167Taking with him all who were to go,
Ramachandra at the parting was distraught at heart.

168The people of the village of Kheturi, losing their composure,
all went with them to the bank of the Padmavati.

169Sri Ishvari, consoling all the people,
wholly without composure, boarded the boat.

170Sri Thakura Mahashaya said to the helmsman:
"Take the boat quickly across the Padma."

171The helmsman brought the boat across the Padma,
and the people here went back distraught to the village.

172On the bank of the Padmavati the Ishvari with everyone
bathed and quickly came to Budhari.

173The people of the nearby villages there
came running to see her.

174Seeing all the mahantas, they
could not restrain their hearts and were bathed in tears.

175Seeing them so, the wise ones rejoiced
and addressed them in the sweetest words.

176Sri Ishvari with everyone, with gladness of heart,
stayed in a wonderful secluded lodging.

177Sri Govinda Kaviraja asked the cooks
to go and cook.

178They quickly and joyfully cooked,
offered the food to Krishna and removed it.

179Sri Ishvari, cooking very briefly,
offered it to Krishna with milk and so on,

180removed the offering, ate happily,
bathed again and sat on her seat.

181Meanwhile the cooks with great care
fed all the mahantas.

182Sri Thakura Mahashaya and all the others
ate together with the cooks.

183What bliss the Ishvari felt that day:
she arranged the marriage of Baru Gangadasa!

184Baru Gangadasa, the crown of the renounced,
who has no desire even in dreams,

185was very abashed, but
married by the Ishvari's will.5

186How Jahnava Ishvari arranged the marriage
I cannot describe for fear of the book's length.

187A lovely Deity named Shyamaraya —
what a wondrous pose, how lovely in every limb! —

188said to the Ishvari in a dream:
"Now entrust Me to Baru Gangadasa."

189At the command in the dream, the Ishvari with great joy
gave the service to Baru Gangadasa.

190At once she established the order of offerings,
and the next day there was a great festival.

191What the Ishvari told Baru Gangadasa in private
I cannot understand.

192Leaving Baru Gangadasa in the village of Budhari,
she came with everyone to Kantaka-nagara.

193Sri Yadunandana and others, with joyful hearts,
came out to meet them and brought them to Prabhu's house.

194As Prabhu, having eaten, was about to rest,
at that moment all entered the courtyard.

195Seeing Gaurachandra with great joy at heart,
she stayed with everyone in the former lodging.

196Sri Thakura Mahashaya and all the others
were given wonderful lodgings in complete seclusion.

197All went to bathe in the Ganga,
and meanwhile all the provisions were made ready.

198A man was sent quickly to Yajigrama,
and Sri Acharya Thakura came with everyone.

199Meanwhile all, having bathed and done their rites,
ate a few prasada sweets.

200At that moment the Acharya arrived,
and seeing him, all rejoiced.

201Srinivasa Acharya bowed to all,
and all, bowing, embraced Srinivasa.

202Affectionately they asked Srinivasa of his welfare;
Srinivasa said: "This darshan is my welfare."

203All who were with Srinivasa
bowed at the feet of all the mahantas.

204All the mahantas did as was fitting;
the affection they showed I cannot describe.

205Meanwhile the cooks cooked,
offered the food to Krishna and removed it.

206Sri Ishvari, quickly and briefly cooking,
fed Prabhu and carefully ate herself.

207Bathing again, she said to everyone:
"The day is ending; sit down to eat."

208Taking Srinivasa Acharya and all the others,
all the mahantas ate joyfully.

209Having rinsed their mouths, all sat on their seats,
and the Acharya went to have darshan of the Ishvari.

210He bowed to the ground at the Ishvari's feet,
and the Ishvari affectionately asked of his welfare.

211Srinivasa said: "By the darshan of these feet
all ill fortune of so many days has gone far away."

212Sri Ishvari again, in the sweetest words,
told Srinivasa everything from beginning to end.

213Srinivasa listened with gladness of heart
and came to the lodging of his dear Narottama.

214Sri Govinda Kaviraja told him
all that the Sri Gosvamis had bidden him say.

215Hearing it, the Acharya thought within himself:
"Shall I ever see Prabhu's lotus feet again?"6

216After a while Ramachandra Kaviraja
gave the Acharya the Gopala-virudavali.

217The Acharya took it and placed it on his head,
and then went quickly to see the evening arati.

218All the mahantas came together into the courtyard,
and at the darshan of the arati there was supreme bliss.

219For a while they sang the sankirtana of the name;
the bliss there was cannot be described.

220Sri Jahnava Ishvari, in Prabhu's temple,
lost her composure at the darshan of Prabhu.

221Calming herself with effort, she went to her lodging;
after a while Gauranga retired to rest.

222All the mahantas, taking Srinivasa Acharya,
went to the lodging, overwhelmed with bliss.

223For a while they spoke of Sri Vrindavana;
it grew very late, and they lay down.

224Srinivasa Acharya and others went to their lodging,
and the Acharya lay down with a distraught heart.

225He slept a little, and at the end of the night
Sri Gopala Bhatta appeared to him in a dream.

226Srinivasa fell rolling on the ground
and washed his lotus feet with the tears of his eyes.

227Sri Bhatta Gosvami embraced him firmly
and spoke sweet words to Srinivasa:

228"I am always near you;
birth after birth you are my chief servant."

229Saying many such things, placing his feet on his head,
he vanished — and he came to his senses.

230Meditating on the lotus feet of Sri Gopala Bhatta,
he rose and sat up, remembering Krishna Chaitanya.

231Morning came; all, having done their morning duties,
joyfully bathed in the Suradhuni.

232Having seen Sri Gauranga, they saw Bharati's place too;
in taking leave their hearts were distraught.

233Saying many things to Sri Yadunandana and calming him,
Sri Ishvari came with everyone to Yajigrama.

234Acharya Thakura sent a man to Khanda;
hearing the news, the people of Khanda rejoiced.

235Sri Raghunandana came to Yajigrama
and saw Sri Jahnava Ishvari.

236The gladness there was at meeting everyone
I cannot describe here at length.

237He stayed a while in Yajigrama
and, hearing the accounts of Vraja, lost his composure.

238Again, taking Acharya Srinivasa with him,
he said to the Ishvari in soft words:

239"I have heard everything: there must be no delay;
you must go quickly to Khardaha.

240Tomorrow morning please come to Khanda;
I must go there now."

241Saying this and bowing, he set out for Shrikhanda,
having first asked leave of each of the mahantas.

242Addressing Srinivasa Acharya and all the others,
Sri Raghunandana came joyfully to Khanda.

243He had all the provisions prepared
and the lodgings cleaned at once.

244He saw that everything everywhere was ready;
the people of Khanda were eager for darshan.

245Meanwhile in Yajigrama the Ishvari with everyone
quickly finished the meal and so on.

246The Acharya read from a book for a while,
and after that there was a wondrous sankirtana.

247That day in Yajigrama there was no end to happiness;
what shall I describe? The fortunate saw it.

248At dawn, having done her morning duties,
the Ishvari came with everyone to Shrikhanda.

249The people of Khanda were overwhelmed with bliss,
seeing the two feet of Sri Jahnava.

250The bliss there was at the darshan of all the mahantas —
what shall I describe? Whoever saw it knows.

251Going quickly with everyone to Prabhu's courtyard,
their hearts rejoiced at the darshan of Prabhu.

252Where Prabhu Nityananda danced,
where in prema he drank honey,7

253where Nitai watched Narahari's dancing,
where he became grey with dust —

254seeing all those places with gladness of heart,
all stayed in a most wonderful lodging.

255That day the cooking was finished quickly;
offering it quickly to Prabhu, all ate.

256Knowing the Ishvari's wish, Sri Raghunandana
began a sankirtana that blesses the world.

257In the sankirtana a wondrous flood of prema arose;
all swam, and no one's mind was steady.

258All forgot themselves;
someone clasped another's feet and wept;

259they rolled on the ground, overwhelmed at heart,
and everyone's body grew grey with dust.

260As the song and music were, so was the dancing:
at it a heart like stone melts.

261Someone, standing to one side, said to another:
"There is no comparison for the song, dance and music."

262Someone said: "O brother, I feel I shall die,
taking on myself the misfortunes of this dance, song and music!"

263Someone said: "In the ocean of song, dance and music
only he drowns to whom they give their mercy."

264Saying this, drenched with streams of tears,
they went about like maddened elephants.

265In the wondrous ecstasy of such a sweet kirtana
they remembered nothing — the night came to an end.

266By Prabhu's will, growing calm after a while,
all came to the lodgings and rested.

267They slept a little, and the night turned to morning;
all quickly finished their morning duties and so on.

268The Ishvari quickly bathed and did her rites
and fed Prabhu with wonderful cooking.

269At the Ishvari's command all — Madhava Acharya and others
together with Sri Raghunandana — sat down to eat.

270The Ishvari herself served;
I do not know with what bliss all ate.

271Sri Jahnava Ishvari, having fed everyone,
ate last of all, with love.

272At the Ishvari's affection Sri Raghunandana
lost his composure and could not check his tears.

273The people of the village of Shrikhanda, by the Ishvari's virtues,
were overwhelmed; their happiness grew moment by moment.

274Sri Ishvari, having joyfully bathed again,
sat with Srinivasa Acharya and others

275and said in the sweetest words, with great affection:
"From here all of you go quickly to Kheturi.

276I shall set out for Khardaha tomorrow morning;
from there I shall send news quickly."

277Saying many such things, they came to Prabhu's courtyard,
and there was bliss at the darshan of the evening arati.

278After listening for a while to the singing of the name,
she took leave and went to her lodging.

279Sri Raghunandana and others, before the Ishvari,
said something in sweet words:

280"We have heard you will leave tomorrow morning;
we cannot keep you now by insisting.

281You are independent — we are afraid to ask,
but it would be good if you came from time to time.

282There is no one as shameless as I:
burning in such a fire of separation, I still live."

283Hearing such words of Raghunandana,
the Ishvari lost her composure; streams flowed from both her eyes.

284After a while Sri Raghunandana, growing calm,
came, having said many humble words,

285and gave everyone Gauranga's prasada provisions;
though not hungry, all ate.

286What he gave at once to go with Sri Ishvari
he entrusted to Sri Madhava Acharya.

287It grew very late, and they lay down;
when the night turned to morning, all took leave.

288How distraught everyone's heart was at that time,
what tears flowed — who has the power to describe it?

289By the road by which Shrimati Ishvari had come before,
by that road, visiting everyone, she went to Khardaha.

290How the Ishvari went, how people came and went —
what power have I to describe all that?

291Meanwhile in Khanda Sri Thakura Raghunandana,
with the Acharya and others, was overwhelmed with prema.

292That day the Acharya and others stayed there,
and in the morning, taking leave, they came to Yajigrama.

293Staying two or four days in Yajigrama,
he went quickly to Nadia with two companions.

294How they went about Navadvipa
is told at length in the book Bhakti-ratnakara.

295From there Sri Acharya, coming back to Yajigrama,
spent that night in sankirtana.

296The next day he set out in the morning
and in four or five days came to the village of Budhari.

297Leaving Sri Govinda Kaviraja and some others there,
the next day he came to Kheturi.

298Hearing of his coming, people ran from all sides
and saw him with great gladness of heart.

299Acharya Thakura and Sri Thakura Mahashaya
gladdened them all with sweet words.

300Going quickly with everyone to Gauranga's courtyard,
they had darshan, wholly losing their composure.

301At that moment a letter came from Khardaha;
reading the letter, they learned that all was well.

302At once writing a letter of supreme good news,
they sent it with great joy to Khardaha.

303After staying there a while, they came to the lodging
and day and night were intoxicated with talk of Krishna.

304Every day was like a great festival —
I cannot describe it for fear of length.

305The Acharya, Sri Mahashaya and Ramachandra, the three —
what they spoke of in private I do not know.

306Sri Acharya, staying fifteen days,
went by way of Budhari to Kanchanagadiya.

307There he stayed five days in supreme bliss
and with many disciples came to Yajigrama.

308Continually he taught everyone the shastras of bhakti;
no one had the power to dispute with him.

309Among all he roared like a maddened lion,
and hearing him, the logicians and others fled far away.

310People came from various lands to study
and went home as teachers of the books of bhakti.

311The great treasure of prema-bhakti, rare even for the gods,
he distributes by Sri Chaitanya's will.

312Sinners and pashandis, by the Acharya's mercy,
sing Sri Krishna Chaitanya's virtues continually.

313Not different in body from such a Sri Acharya,
Sri Thakura Narottama, an ocean of virtues,

314with Ramachandra, dearer than life,
enjoys the festivity of prema in the village of Sri Kheturi.

315The Srimad-Bhagavata and the Gosvamis' books
he continually has his disciples study.

316Hearing his explanations of the books of bhakti, karmis and jnanis
become Vaishnavas and condemn karma and jnana.

317Brahmanas and Vaishnavas from other lands, coming together,
study the Gosvamis' books and teach them everywhere.

318So he distributes the jewels of the books of bhakti;
fortunate people hear of this.

319One day Narottama with Ramachandra
sat speaking of Krishna.

320At that moment a distinguished brahmana came
and said to the Mahashaya, weeping:

321"Before my students, in my pride,
I said so much that it cannot be repeated.

322From the day I regarded you as a shudra,
I was struck with leprosy.

323To cure the disease I took many medicines,
performed rites for welfare to Shiva and much else.

324Instead of a cure my torment grew,
and I resolved to enter the Ganga.8

325In a dream Bhagavati, turning away from me,
said in anger: 'A special misfortune awaits you.

326In your pride you regarded Narottama as a shudra;
your study and learning have turned your mind to ashes.

327Whoever regards Narottama as an ordinary man —
that sinner has no deliverance ever.

328But if he, by your good fortune, is kind to you,
then alone you will be saved — know this for certain.'

329Saying this, she vanished;
morning came, and I came here.

330I was afraid to come before you,
but on the way a wise man said that you are merciful.

331Seeing you from afar,
my eyes were soothed — as if I had found life.

332Forgive my offense this once:
I take shelter at these feet of yours."

333Saying this, he was bathed in the tears of both his eyes,
and, distraught, the brahmana fell to the ground.

334Sri Thakura Mahashaya said again and again:
"You have committed no offense against me."

335The brahmana said: "Place your feet on my head;
only then will this sinner's heart be at peace."

336Narottama, remembering Sri Krishna Chaitanya,
embraced the brahmana in prema.

337The brahmana, embracing him and taking the dust of his feet,
began to dance with both arms raised.

338After a while the brahmana grew calm:
the disease had gone, his body had become clean.

339Prema-bhakti arose in the brahmana's heart,
and when the disease was cured, he thought:

340"It would have been better had the disease stayed in my body:
I fear lest pride should arise again."

341So the brahmana thought, and by the power of bhakti
he became a Vaishnava together with his whole family.

342All this became known everywhere,
and the brahmanas' fear grew immensely.

343Someone said to another: "Be careful:
do not regard Sri Narottama as a shudra."

344Someone said: "Brahmanas, intoxicated with pride,
cannot recognize such a jewel as Narottama."

345Someone said: "Narottama is an abode of mercy:
by his own goodness he mercifully destroys the fear of worldly existence."

346Someone said: "I saw with my own eyes:
by singing Sri Narottama's virtues the low became exalted."

347Someone said: "Narottama is an ocean of virtues:
so many virtues are never possible in a human being."

348Someone said: "He only has a human form:
he is a descent of a part of Ishvara to deliver living beings."

349Saying many such things, the old and worthy brahmanas
each warned their own families.

350They sing Sri Narottama's virtues continually;
what shall I say of all his deeds?

351How the Mahashaya from time to time went to Yajigrama
and spent happy times with the Acharya,

352what his meeting with Vira Hambira was like —
is described in the book Bhakti-ratnakara.

353Listen to all this continually and with care:
Narahari tells the Narottama-vilasa.

Thus ends the ninth vilasa of the Narottama-vilasa.

Notes

  1. Madhupuri is Mathura.
  2. Govinda Kaviraja (Govindadasa), the famous poet of padas, brother of Ramachandra Kaviraja and disciple of Srinivasa.
  3. The Gopala-virudavali is a work of Jiva Gosvami; "this book," which he promises to finish, is apparently the Gopala-champu.
  4. According to tradition, on returning to Gauda Jahnava had a Deity of Radha made and sent it to Gopinatha in Vrindavana; "this one" is the earlier Radha beside Gopinatha. Cf. the Prema-vilasa (ev-jahnava-gopinatha).
  5. Baru (Bara) Gangadasa was a disciple of Gauridasa Pandita; the marriage of a renunciant at Jahnava's will underlines her authority as guru.
  6. That is, of Gopala Bhatta, Srinivasa's guru.
  7. On Nityananda's dancing in Shrikhanda and the cup of honey that became nectar — a tradition of Shrikhanda (cf. BR).
  8. That is, to end his life in the Ganga.
